narrative.overview:
Klunk produces formal, ink-on-paper examinations, so its screens read like a technical document on a drafting table rather than a soft dashboard. Structure comes from thin ruled lines on warm paper, not from shadows or cards floating over a background. Ink is near-black and carries almost everything. Colour is held back for meaning: blueprint blue for what is selected or open, annotation red for anything a teacher has to look at, approval green for what is settled.

The idea began with a Design and Technology faculty and holds for every subject. A trial paper in History is as much a formal document as one in D&T, and the teacher building it is checking a proof, not browsing a feed. Density is moderate: a question list is meant to be scanned at a glance, with marks in tabular figures because marks are the number that matters.

The printed paper is a separate system with its own stylesheet, `print.css`, and shares nothing with this one on purpose. It is black on white A4 and follows examination conventions whatever the screen is doing. This file governs the app's screens only.
keyCharacteristics: Warm drafting paper under a faint ruled grid; white sheets for panels.
Hairline rules (1px) for structure. No drop shadows.
Near-black ink for text and primary actions.
Colour only where it means something, and never as the only signal.
A serif for the masthead, a humanist sans for the interface, monospace for labels, data and code.
System fonts only. The content-security policy loads no web fonts.

rules.name: The Annotation Rule
rules.body: Red marks only what a teacher must look at. If nothing needs checking, nothing on the screen is red, apart from the active tab's underline.

rules.name: The Never Colour Alone Rule
rules.body: Every colour that carries meaning is paired with words or form. A dead tag is struck through and dashed as well as red; a status block says in its own words what it is reporting. This is WCAG 2.2 AA 1.4.1, and it is a floor, not a preference.

rules.name: The Monospace Means Literal Rule
rules.body: Monospace is for labels, numbers, file paths and program code. It is never decoration for looking technical.

rules.name: The Flat Table Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow. A surface that needs to stand out gets a rule or a wash.

rules.name: The Margin Mark Rule
rules.body: A 3px bar down the left edge of a block is a margin mark, and it carries a status: Annotation Red for a fault or a doubt, Blueprint Blue for a note or the thing chosen, Approval Green for settled, Strong Rule for pending. It is always paired with words that say what the status is. A block with no status has no bar. It gets the hairline border every sheet has.

dos: Do structure a screen with hairline rules and white sheets on the drafting paper.
Do keep every clickable or typeable control at 2.35rem, apart from the small in-row variants.
Do give every signal colour a partner in words or form.
Do put marks and counts in tabular figures.
Do keep the grid as the page ground.
Do use a margin mark only on a block that reports a status, and pair it with its words.
donts: Don't use drop shadows, floating cards or nested containers.
Don't use a left bar as decoration. A block with nothing to report gets the hairline border every sheet has.
Don't use red for anything that does not need a teacher's eye.
Don't use monospace to look technical. It is for labels, data and code.
Don't load a web font or any other network resource. The CSP forbids it.
Don't carry these screen styles onto the printed paper, which follows examination conventions in `print.css`.
